description:
## Why

Rather than implementing Exchange protocols (MAPI, EWS — complex, dying, no Rust ecosystem), stoa can bridge to Microsoft 365 mailboxes via the Microsoft Graph API (REST/JSON, OAuth 2.0). This turns stoa into a local/federated mirror of a user's M365 mail with stoa's archival integrity, data sovereignty, and JMAP/IMAP serving on top.

Use cases:
- Organizations on Microsoft 365 that want local archival with cryptographic integrity (eDiscovery, compliance)
- Users who want to own their mail history even if their M365 subscription ends
- Hybrid deployments: M365 as the primary MTA, stoa as the sovereign archive and NNTP layer
- Migration path off M365: sync everything into stoa, then cut over

EWS is deprecated for Exchange Online as of October 2026. Graph is Microsoft's stated replacement and the correct protocol target.

## What

A sync daemon (or stoa-mail subcommand) that:

1. Authenticates to Microsoft Graph via OAuth 2.0 (device code flow or client credentials for unattended operation)
2. Uses Graph delta queries (GET /me/messages?=...) to incrementally sync mail into stoa's block store — only changed/new messages fetched after initial sync
3. Uses Graph webhooks (change notifications) for near-real-time push sync as an alternative to polling
4. Syncs folder hierarchy (GET /me/mailFolders) to newsgroup or JMAP mailbox structure
5. Syncs message flags/keywords (read, flagged, answered) bidirectionally
6. Stores raw RFC 5322 message bytes (fetched via $value endpoint) as CID-addressed blocks in stoa's configured block store
7. Records sync state (delta tokens) in SQLite so restarts resume from the last known position

## Protocol mapping

- Graph mailFolder → JMAP Mailbox / NNTP newsgroup
- Graph message flags (isRead, flag.flagStatus) → JMAP keywords (, )
- Graph delta token → stoa state token (stored in SQLite alongside the account)
- Graph message id → stoa Message-ID header (extracted from raw RFC 5322 bytes)

## Implementation

graph-rs-sdk is a maintained Rust crate for Microsoft Graph with reasonable coverage of mail and calendar endpoints. Use this rather than hand-rolling the Graph HTTP client.

Authentication: Azure app registration required (client ID, tenant ID). For BYOA deployment, customer registers their own Azure app and provides credentials via Secrets Manager.

## Config

```toml
[graph_sync]
enabled = true
client_id = "..."
tenant_id = "..."
# client_secret from Secrets Manager / env var, never in config file
poll_interval_secs = 300   # fallback if webhooks not configured
mailbox = "user@example.com"
target_account_id = "u_alice"  # stoa JMAP account to sync into
```

## Acceptance

- Initial sync pulls all messages from all folders into stoa block store
- Incremental sync via delta tokens fetches only changes since last run
- Sync state survives process restart
- Message flags sync bidirectionally (mark read in stoa → reflected in M365 and vice versa)
- Folder hierarchy maps to JMAP mailboxes
- Integration tests run against Microsoft Graph sandbox / mock (not requiring live M365 credentials in CI)
notes: Calendar and contacts sync via Graph (GET /me/calendars, GET /me/contacts) is out of scope for this issue but is the natural follow-on once mail sync is stable. The Graph delta query pattern is similar to JMAP Email/changes — the concepts map cleanly.
title: Microsoft Graph API sync bridge
